sentences.text: The appellants in FAM No.2/2023 have also challenged the order dated 20.01.2023 passed in Misc. Civil Case No.127/2022 by the Tribunal in the review application.

02. Facts of the case, in brief, are that a proposal was sent from the office of Executive Engineer to the Land Acquisition Officer, Dabhara for acquisition of land for construction of Saradeeh Barrage of 127.06 acres (51.397 hectare) at Village Nawapara, P.H.No.12, Revenue Circle Dabhara, Distt.
Janjgir-Champa in the year 2013.
Upon receipt of such proposal, a land acquisition case was opened and registered as case No.27/A-82/2012-13 by the Land Acquisition Officer.

As the proceedings were under process, meanwhile the old Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was replaced by the new Act namely the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act of 2013") w.e.f. 01.01.2014, as such the Executive Engineer sent requisition to the Land Acquisition Officer seeking amendment in the land acquisition proposal vide letter dated 31.03.2015.

sentences.text: Thereafter, a preliminary notification under Section 11 of the Act was issued on 01.04.2015 and the same was published in the official gazette on 03.04.2015.
Paper publication was also made in two daily newspapers on 07.04.2015.
The publication of notification was also affixed on the public places at the concerned village on 08.04.2015 seeking claims and objections.
However, no objection whatsoever was received as required under Section 15(1) of the Act of 2013.

Therefore, notification under Section 19 of the Act of 2013 was issued on 06.05.2016 whereas publication in newspapers namely Hari Bhoomi, Bilaspur and Moolmantra, Janjgir-Champa was made on 06.04.2016 and publication of the notification in the public places of concerned village was made on 01.04.2016 by pasting it.

03. The public notice under Section 21(1) of the Act of 2013 was issued on 30.05.2016 requiring the affecting parties to raise their objections, if any, however, no objection as required under Section Smt. 3 21(2) of the Act of 2013 was received from any of the land owners or other affected persons.

During the course of scrutiny, it was noticed that there was clerical error in respect of 6 numbers of Khasras whereby total 1.404 hectare area of land could not be included in the land acquisition proceedings

,
therefore, the amended notification under Section 19 of the Act of 2013 was issued on 25.06.2016 and 01.07.2016 and the same was made public by way of paper publication on 25.07.2016 and pasting the same on public places at the concerned village on 04.07.2016.
The Land Acquisition Officer requisitioned Khasra B-1 from the concerned Halka Patwari and summoned the sale-sorts from the Deputy Registrar, Dabhra for the period from 01.04.2012 to 01.04.2015.

It was found that during the relevant period in village Nawapara, there was no sale/purchase transaction for the irrigated land situated at Village Nawapara, therefore, the sale-sorts of Village Upani, P.H. No.12 was taken for further computation and further in accordance with Explanation No.2 under Section 26 of the Act of 2013, value of the irrigated and un-irrigated lands were determined applying the market value guideline for the year 2015-2016 which was also taken into consideration and on due consideration of the proper value, the applicable compensation for land was arrived at.

The final award was passed on 31.03.2017 against which Smt. Padum Kunwar and Smt. Mongara Devi raised objections and moved application before the Land Acquisition Officer seeking reference to be placed before the competent authority under Section 64 of the Act of 2013.

04. On receiving the application for reference, the Land Acquisition Officer referred the matter to the Presiding Officer vide memo dated 04.08.2017 and thereafter, the Presiding Officer opened and registered the case bearing Reference Case No.179/2017.

Learned Presiding Officer after considering the pleadings of the respective parties and the evidence on record, allowed the reference petition with a direction that the compensation amount shall carry interest @ 9% per annum from January,
2013 for a period of one year and for remaining period @ 15% to be paid within a period of two months from the date of receipt of the order.

Aggrieved by the award dated 15.09.2022, the appellants in FAM No.02/2023 preferred a review application under Section 60(1)
(f) of the Act of 2013 which was rejected by order dated 20.01.2023.
Hence these appeals.

05. Learned counsel for the appellant in FAM No.01/2023 would argue that the award dated 15.09.2022 to the extent of awarding interest under Section 80 of the Act of 2013 from January,
2013 is per se illegal, bad and perverse, as such required to be set aside.

Learned Presiding Officer grossly failed to appreciate that the land acquisition proceedings commence from the date of issuance of preliminary notification which in the instant case was 03.04.2015 and therefore,
computation of award can only cover the period from 03.04.2015 and onwards.
Only the process was initiated prior to 03.04.2015 when proposal was sent by the appellant/State.

However, by misinterpretation of the statement made by witness namely Virendra Kanwar who in his cross-examination admitted that the construction of Saradeeh Barrage was started from the year 2011, the impugned order has been passed in favour of respondents No. 1 to 3.

Although the construction part of Saradeeh Barrage commenced in the year 2011, but there was no material to substantiate that from the date of initiation of construction of barrage since 2011 there was any obstruction in the agricultural works of respondents No. 1 to 3 due to it because the construction of barrage work starts from laying the foundation and such activities are first initiated under the river.
More so, the adjoining lands only get submerged when the sluice gate of the Barrage is closed.

In the Smt. Padum Kunwar (Died) Through Lrs- vs Executive Engineer on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105117001/
4 instant case, the land of respondents No. 1 to 3 remained unaffected and as per written statement of the appellant and respondent No.4, at least till the date of filing their written statements, the sluice gates were not closed, hence no portion of agricultural lands belonging to respondents No. 1 to 3 ever submerged.

sentences.text: Learned Presiding Officer ought to have called for report from the concerned Halka Patwari particularly in respect of the area under agricultural cultivation of the concerned village Nawapara.

Learned Presiding Officer has grossly failed to examine the issue properly as for want of proper reports from the concerned Halka Patwari, only on the basis of oral statement, it was wrongly assumed that the lands of respondents No. 1 to 3 were put under submergence since the year 2013.

Learned counsel for the appellant would further contend that the learned Presiding Officer miserably failed to consider and appreciate the fact that interest part as required under the provisions of the Act of 2013 was already calculated in the final award of compensation as was submitted by both the appellant and respondent No.4 in their written statement.

Compensation amount including interest from 03.04.2015 to 31.03.2017 was already computed and respondents No. 1 to 3 were issued notices by respondent No.4 in accordance with law asking them to receive the compensation amount which was not received by them, therefore, delay in making payment of compensation cannot be attributed either to the appellant or respondent No.4.

Learned Presiding Officer erred by not appreciating the fact that the reference case was preferred by respondents No. 1 to 3 on account of inter-se dispute amongst themselves in respect of apportionment of the land and hence the award amount was not received by them despite it being available with the Land Acquisition Officer.
Thus, there was no delay on the part of the appellant or respondent No.4 in disbursement of compensation amount and as such, respondents No. 1 to 3 were not entitled for any interest.
Therefore, the impugned award dated 15.09.2022 to the extent of awarding interest under Section 80 of the Act of 2013 from January, 2013 may be set aside in the interest of justice.

06. Opposing the above contention of learned counsel for the appellant/State, learned counsel for the appellants in FAM No.02/2023 would submit that under Section 77 of the Act of 2013, which is mandatory in nature, respondent No.1 has not paid compensation till filing of the petition or deposited before the concerned authority, even otherwise also though respondent No.1 is not aggrieved by the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer and has not preferred any reference,
has not deposited the amount of compensation as per award dated 31.03.2017 till date and on reference being made by the appellants, award has been modified to some extent, then also the Tribunal in reference and in review has failed to impose penal interest @ 3% as the appellants were deprived of their human as well as constitutional rights under Article 300-A of the Constitution of India.

As per judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Reddy Veerana Vs. State of UP, AIR 2022 SC 2225, the appellants are not only entitled for interest under Section 80 of the Act of 2013 till actual payment, but also additional interest @ 3% per annum from the date of taking of possession till actual payment.

07. As regards court fees in FAM No.2/2023, learned counsel for the appellants submits that they have filed an application (IA No.4/2023) in this regard.

He argued that the appellants have mainly challenged the non-compliance of statutory requirement and not the award for re- fixation of any Smt. Padum Kunwar (Died) Through Lrs- vs Executive Engineer on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105117001/
5

market value of land which has already been determined and adjudicated by the authorities and additional amount of 12% on market value under Section 30(3) of the Act of 2013 is a solatium and not a part of the award and is a statutory provision required to be followed and determined.
Therefore, no court fee is payable on the difference of the solatium to which the appellants are legally entitled under Section 30(3) of the Act of 2013.
Likewise, for the relief of non- grant of penal interest for delayed payment and non-compliance of Section 80 of the Act of 2013, no court fees is payable on interest.
As such, the default pointed out by the Registry deserves to be overruled.

Reliance has been placed on the decisions in the matters of Assistant Commissioner, Gadag Sub Division, Gadag Vs. Mathapathi Basavannewwa and others, (1995) AIR (SC) 2492; Dhiraj Ambalal Patel Vs. State of Gujarat, 2019 SCC OnLine Guj 3865; Gayabai Digambar Puri (died) thr. LR Vs.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State vehemently opposes the prayer of the appellants in FAM No.2/2023 and submits that the appellants have not paid requisite court fees and therefore, the appeal (FAM No.2/2023) is not maintainable.
The Registry has also pointed out this default, as such the appellants have to deposit the proper court fees or else the appeal is liable to be dismissed for want of proper court fee.
It is well settled law of the land that court fee would be levied on solatium in land acquisition matters.
The solatium is statutory compensation payable to the land owner for the compulsory acquisition of his land.
This appeal is not maintainable as no requisite court fee has been paid by the appellants and no application under Section 149 of CPC has been filed.

Therefore,
this appeal is not tenable and liable to be dismissed.

09. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
10.
In FAM No.2/2023, the appellants have claimed the following relief:

"It is, therefore, prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to allow this appeal and further be pleased to modify the impugned award dated 15/09/2022 (Annexure A/1) and also hold that the order passed in review dated 20/01/2023 is perverse and the appellants are entitled for claim as made in the original claim application with other relief as deem fit may also be passed, in the interest of justice."
11.

Sections 30, 69, 70 and 80 of the Act of 2013 read as under:
"Section 30. Award of solatium.
(1) The Collector having determined the total compensation to be paid, shall, to arrive at the final award, impose a "Solatium" amount equivalent to one hundred per cent.
of the compensation amount.

sentences.text: 6 Explanation.---For the removal of doubts
it is hereby declared that solatium amount shall be in addition to the compensation payable to any person whose land has been acquired.
(2) The Collector shall issue individual awards detailing the particulars of compensation payable and the details of payment of the compensation as specified in the First Schedule.

(3) In addition to the market value of the land provided under section 26, the Collector shall, in every case, award an amount calculated at the rate of twelve per cent. per annum on such market value for the period commencing on and from the date of the publication of the notification of the Social Impact Assessment study under sub-section (2) of section 4, in respect of such land, till the date of the award of the Collector or the date of taking possession of the land, whichever is earlier."
"Section 69. Determination of award by Authority.

(1) In determining the amount of compensation to be awarded for land acquired including the Rehabilitation and Resettlement entitlements, the Authority shall take into consideration whether the Collector has followed the parameters set out under section 26 to section 30 and the provisions under Chapter V of this Act.

(2) In addition to the market value of the land, as above provided, the Authority shall in every case award an amount calculated at the rate of twelve per cent. per annum on such market value for the period commencing on and from the date of the publication of the preliminary notification under section 11 in respect of such land to the date of the award of the Collector or the date of taking possession of the land,
whichever is earlier.

Explanation.--In computing the period referred to in this sub- section, any period or periods during which the proceedings for the acquisition of the land were held up on account of any stay or injunction by the order of any Court shall be excluded.
(3) In addition to the market value of the land as above provided, the Authority shall in every case award a solatium of one hundred per cent.
over the total compensation amount."
"Section 70. Form of award.

(1) Every award under this Chapter shall be in writing signed by the Presiding Officer of the Authority, and shall specify the amount awarded under clause first of section 28, and also the amounts (if any) respectively awarded under each of the other clauses of the same subsection, together with the grounds of awarding each of the said amounts.

. (2) Every such award shall be deemed to be a decree and the statement of the grounds of every such award a judgment within the meaning of clause (2), and clause (9) of respectively, of section 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908)."

"Section 80. Payment of interest.

When the amount of such compensation is not paid or deposited on or before taking possession of the land, the Collector shall pay the amount awarded with interest thereon at the rate of nine per cent.

per annum shall be payable from the date or expiry of the said period of one year on the amount of compensation or part thereof which has not been paid or deposited before the date of such expiry."
As per Gazette Notification dated 9.2.2016 in case of rural areas, the factor by which the market value is to be multiplied shall be 2.00.

Notification dated 9.2.2016 reads as under:
"NOTIFICATION New Delhi, the 9th February, 2016 S.O. 425 (E) - In exercise of the powers conferred by column no.3 of serial no. 2 of the First Schedule read with sub-section (2) of section 30 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (No. 30 of 2013), the Central Government, hereby, notifies that in case of rural areas, the factor by which the market value is to be multiplied shall be 2.00 (two).

12. Looking to the above provisions and the relief claimed by the appellants, it is clear that the appellants filed this appeal (FAM No.2/2023) for modification of the order and calculation of interest as per Section 30(3) of the Act of 2013 and against non-compliance of Section 80 of the Act of 2013.
The appellants are not claiming any enhancement of award.

Therefore, in view of the afore-quoted provisions of the Act and the nature of relief claimed by the appellants, the application (IA No.04/2023) is allowed and the office objection regarding payment of court fees is hereby overruled.

13. It is not in dispute in this case that the lands of the appellants in FAM No.2/2023 and other land owners were acquired by the State and award was passed on 31.3.2017 by the Sub Divisional Officer,
Dabhra, Distt. Janjgir-Champa.

The appellants filed an application before the SDO (R) and Land Acquisition Officer, Dabhra and based on that, the the Land Acquisition Officer, Dabhra sent a reference dated 4.8.2017 to the Land Acquisition, Resettlement and Rehabilitation Tribunal for deciding the same.

15. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Gayabai Digambar Puri (supra) held as under:
"It is well-settled that the normal rule is that if on account of acquisition of land a person is deprived of possession of his property, he should be paid compensation immediately and if the same is not paid to him forthwith, he would be entitled to interest on the compensation amount from the date of taking possession of the land till the date of payment thereof as expounded in R.L. 19. This Court in the matter of Smt. Anita Agrawal (supra) observed in paras 9, 10, 11 & 12 of the order as under:
"9.

Keeping the above arguments and the stand of the State taking their return, we are hot satisfied with the so- called explanation offered as to why a multiplier of 100 as a thumb rule should be used for the entire State of Chhattisgarh.
The very object and purpose behind the variable component between 1.00 and 2.00 has been lost, if not robbed.

sentences.text: Further, the question is not about the power of the State Government to issue such notification, the question is the manner in which such power has been exercised which can also be levelled as mindless exercise of power since by restricting the multiplier factor to 1.00, the State is obviously trying to treat all land owners as one.
This will deny to the poor land owners of the remote villages, fair compensation and rehabilitation, which is the primary object behind the new Land Acquisition Act of 2013.

11. Drawing analogy from the view taken by the Division Bench of Bombay High Court, which we have quoted with due approval, Court is left with no option but to strike down the notification dated 04.12.2014 contained in Annexure P/1. A direction is issued that keeping in mind the legal position which emerges, the State Government will issue a fresh notification indicating the multiplier factors, in terms of the guidelines laid down in the statue and the judgment.

entities.text: Division Bench of Bombay High Court

sentences.text: 12. It goes without saying that all awards and compensations in relation to not only these Petitioners but all such persons whose lands have been acquired and a multiplier of 1.00 has been used for calculating the compensation, the same will be required to be revised and revisited in light of the new notification, which is required to be notified by the State Government, on priority."
20. In view of the above, in the present case it is evident from the letter dated 21.8.2024 that till this date no compensation was paid to the land owners.
It is not disputed that as per notification dated 9.2.2016, in case of rural areas, multiplier of 2 is applicable by which the market value is to be multiplied.
In the present case, the award was passed on 31.3.2017 and therefore, the multiplier of two is applicable.

21. In view of above, the findings recorded by the learned Tribunal in para 16 of the award are not according to the amended notification and it is held that multiplier of two is applicable in this case.
However, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the Tribunal rightly found that the land owners are dispossessed from their lands since 2013 and calculated interest since 2013.

22. On the basis of aforesaid discussions:
 FAM No.1 of 2023 filed by the appellant/State being without any substance is hereby dismissed.
 FAM No.2 of 2023 filed by the appellants/land owners is allowed in part.
It is ordered that the applicable multiplied in this case is two and hence calculation be made accordingly.
The impugned award stands modified to the above extent only.

The respondent authorities shall pay the above amount and proportionate interest to the appellants after adjusting the amount already paid to them, within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
No order as to costs.

opennyai_summary.facts:
As the proceedings were under process, meanwhile the old Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was replaced by the new Act namely the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act of 2013") w.e.f. 01.01.2014, as such the Executive Engineer sent requisition to the Land Acquisition Officer seeking amendment in the land acquisition proposal vide letter dated 31.03.2015.
04. On receiving the application for reference, the Land Acquisition Officer referred the matter to the Presiding Officer vide memo dated 04.08.2017 and thereafter, the Presiding Officer opened and registered the case bearing Reference Case No.179/2017.
Learned Presiding Officer after considering the pleadings of the respective parties and the evidence on record, allowed the reference petition with a direction that the compensation amount shall carry interest @ 9% per annum from January,
2013 for a period of one year and for remaining period @ 15% to be paid within a period of two months from the date of receipt of the order.
Aggrieved by the award dated 15.09.2022, the appellants in FAM No.02/2023 preferred a review application under Section 60(1)
(f) of the Act of 2013 which was rejected by order dated 20.01.2023.
Only the process was initiated prior to 03.04.2015 when proposal was sent by the appellant/State.
Although the construction part of Saradeeh Barrage commenced in the year 2011, but there was no material to substantiate that from the date of initiation of construction of barrage since 2011 there was any obstruction in the agricultural works of respondents No. 1 to 3 due to it because the construction of barrage work starts from laying the foundation and such activities are first initiated under the river.
More so, the adjoining lands only get submerged when the sluice gate of the Barrage is closed.
Learned Presiding Officer ought to have called for report from the concerned Halka Patwari particularly in respect of the area under agricultural cultivation of the concerned village Nawapara.
Learned Presiding Officer has grossly failed to examine the issue properly as for want of proper reports from the concerned Halka Patwari, only on the basis of oral statement, it was wrongly assumed that the lands of respondents No. 1 to 3 were put under submergence since the year 2013.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Learned Presiding Officer grossly failed to appreciate that the land acquisition proceedings commence from the date of issuance of preliminary notification which in the instant case was 03.04.2015 and therefore,
computation of award can only cover the period from 03.04.2015 and onwards.
Learned Presiding Officer erred by not appreciating the fact that the reference case was preferred by respondents No. 1 to 3 on account of inter-se dispute amongst themselves in respect of apportionment of the land and hence the award amount was not received by them despite it being available with the Land Acquisition Officer.
Thus, there was no delay on the part of the appellant or respondent No.4 in disbursement of compensation amount and as such, respondents No. 1 to 3 were not entitled for any interest.
Therefore, the impugned award dated 15.09.2022 to the extent of awarding interest under Section 80 of the Act of 2013 from January, 2013 may be set aside in the interest of justice.
market value of land which has already been determined and adjudicated by the authorities and additional amount of 12% on market value under Section 30(3) of the Act of 2013 is a solatium and not a part of the award and is a statutory provision required to be followed and determined.
Therefore, no court fee is payable on the difference of the solatium to which the appellants are legally entitled under Section 30(3) of the Act of 2013.
It is well settled law of the land that court fee would be levied on solatium in land acquisition matters.
The solatium is statutory compensation payable to the land owner for the compulsory acquisition of his land.
This appeal is not maintainable as no requisite court fee has been paid by the appellants and no application under Section 149 of CPC has been filed.
